key_insight: Orthogonalized momentum can fail on nonsmooth convex problems when momentum is fixed, but becomes reliable when momentum is adaptive and coupled with vanishing step sizes.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued optimization in deep learning and LLM training, MAGD offers a practical Muon-style update that preserves convergence guarantees in nonsmooth settings.
method: Show a failure case for Muon with fixed momentum on convex Lipschitz objectives, even with bounded iterates.
Prove asymptotic convergence for adaptive-momentum Muon under boundedness and regularity assumptions.
Introduce MAGD, which blends orthogonalized momentum and gradient based on relative progress, with an O(min{m,n} ε^-2) convex rate.
evidence_signal: The paper validates the method on synthetic problems, image classification, and LLM pretraining, showing it is a simple and practical alternative to Muon.
watch_item: Performance and guarantees depend on adaptive momentum, vanishing step sizes, and boundedness/regularity assumptions, so fixed-momentum implementations may still be unstable.
